a little noun

also pinch, a bit, a little bit, a tiny bit, a little more, a little bigger, a little of, a little longer, a little strength

classical

Traupman 340

paulum, paulī n.

noun, second declension, with a genitive (paulum silvae); with verbs, an adverb · Declension on Wiktionary

paulum cinnamōmī is our easy way to say “a pinch of cinnamon,” without implying an exact measure. With a verb it is an adverb: paulum redormiō, I sleep a little more.

Other words

  • paululum, paululī n. — a tiny bit, a very little

    noun, second declension (diminutive of paulum); also an adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Curc. 1.2.31: dē paulō paululum hoc tibi dabō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 340 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • paulō (+ comparative) — a little (with comparatives): a little more, a little earlier

    adverb (the ablative of the measure of difference) · also used · classical · Plaut. Men. 4.3.7: paulō prius (Lewis & Short); Cic. Or. 82: līberius paulō (Lewis & Short) · Wiktionary

    With comparatives and with ante, post: paulō prius, a little earlier; paulō post, a little later. “Much more” is multō (see a lot).

Examples

  • paulum cinnamōmī

    a pinch of cinnamoncomposed

  • Nimis acida est? Paulum banānae addāmus.

    Is it too sour? Let’s add a little banana.composed

  • Prō peccātō magnō paulum supplicī satis est patrī.

    For a great wrong, a little punishment is enough for a father.Ter. And. 903

  • hoc erat in vōtīs: modus agrī nōn ita magnus, hortus ubi et tēctō vīcīnus jūgis aquae fōns et paulum silvae super hīs foret

    this is what I prayed for: a piece of land not so very big, with a garden, a spring of running water near the house, and a bit of woodland above themHor. S. 2.6.1–3

  • paulum redormiō, dein ambulō

    I sleep a little more, then go for a walkPlin. Ep. 9.36.3

  • cum autem paulum firmitātis accessit

    but once they have gained a little strengthCic. Fin. 5.42

  • paulō amplior

    a little biggerTraupman 340

See also handful, add, a lot, too little, some, the more …, the more ….
